We need to determine SMILES of whole compound given fragments: aromatic fragment c1ccc(cc1)C(=O)O (that's benzoic acid) and CCCC (butyl chain). Need to connect them somehow to match formula C11H14O2, DBE 5, aromatic carbons 6, carbonyl 1, CH3 groups 1, total carbon 11, hydrogens 14, oxygens 2.

Benzoic acid fragment: C7H6O2 (C6 aromatic + carbonyl carbon + OH). Actually benzoic acid formula C7H6O2. The other fragment CCCC is butyl: C4H9 (if attached as substituent). Combine: total C11 H15 O2? Wait C7H6O2 + C4H9 = C11H15O2. But we need H14. So maybe the butyl is attached via loss of H (i.e., as substituent replacing the OH? Actually benzoic acid has COOH; maybe the butyl is attached to the carbonyl carbon as an ester? That would be butyl benzoate: C6H5-COO-Butyl. Formula: C6H5COO- (C7H5O2) + C4H9 = C11H14O2. Yes that matches. So the compound is butyl benzoate (phenyl carbonyl O-alkyl). SMILES: "CCCCOC(=O)c1ccccc1". Check: aromatic carbon count 6, carbonyl 1, CH3 groups: there is one CH3 at end of butyl chain (CH3-CH2-CH2-CH2-O-). That's one CH3. Number of unique H environments: likely 5 (aromatic protons 5? Actually phenyl has 5 distinct? In para? But in benzoate, aromatic protons are 5 unique? Actually phenyl attached to carbonyl, symmetry gives 5 unique? The ring has 5 distinct H (positions 2-6). plus CH2 next to O, CH2 middle, CH2 next to CH3, CH3 = total 5 types? Wait CH2 next to O is distinct, middle CH2 distinct, CH2 next to CH3 distinct, CH3 distinct, aromatic protons maybe all equivalent? In para? No, phenyl attached to carbonyl, the ring is monosubstituted, so all 5 aromatic H are chemically equivalent? In monosubstituted benzene, all aromatic H are equivalent (they are same environment). So that gives 1 aromatic H type. So total H types: aromatic (1), O-CH2 (1), CH2 (middle) (1), CH2 (next) (1), CH3 (1) = 5. matches.

Carbonyl groups 1, aromatic carbons 6, DBE: aromatic ring 4 DBE, carbonyl 1 =5. matches.

Thus SMILES is "CCCCOC(=O)c1ccccc1". Validate? Use validate_smiles.
